messages:
support_julia: FYI customer acme-prod reports sudden latency spike and auth errors. They expected eu-central but a large fraction of traffic started landing in us-west ~2h ago. Some requests 403, RTT ~220ms. Logs + config attached below.

anya: Can you paste the routing decision logs + the failover policy snapshot? Any recent console edits?

support_julia: Ticket INC-4729. Customer edited their routing policy via Console at 2026-03-17T10:12:00Z (they said they only toggled sessionPin). Repro curl we ran: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "X-Region: eu-central" \ 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Response headers show "x-routed-region: us-west" and body sometimes 403. From the proxy logs: 
```
[10:14:21Z] request_id=abc123 region_hint=eu-central route_decision=fallback->us-west priority_index=1
[10:14:21Z] upstream_status=403 upstream_err="auth mismatch: key-region eu vs routing us-west"
```
Config snapshot from customer (post-save): 
```
failover_policy: {
  "priority": ["us-west","eu-central"],
  "sticky": true,
  "sessionPin": true,
  "weights": {"us-west": 70, "eu-central": 30}
}
```
They say the previous policy before their edit had eu-central first.

derek: That priority array being reversed is suspicious. Did the Console show the same ordering after the save?

support_julia: Customer says Console preview still showed eu-central first, but backend shows us-west first. They only toggled sessionPin from false->true.

matt_sre: I'm also seeing a TTL/cookie mismatch on sessions created after the edit. sessionPin true sets a session cookie domain that our router uses to sticky-route. If the cookie key we set differs from the routing key, the sticky check fails and falls back to priority order. Combined with the reversed priority array that explains the surge to us-west.

ops-bot: Deploy-bot: routing-config-service v5.0.2 deployed 2026-03-17T09:58:13Z to prod (console API).

anya: Likely sequence: console change toggled sessionPin -> console save path serializes the failover object incorrectly and reverses the priority array -> sticky checks inconsistent due to cookie name change -> clients lose affinity and system falls back to first priority (now us-west). We need a repro and quick rollback.

support_julia: Repro steps I ran locally: edit a policy in Console, tick sessionPin, save. Then call the list API `/v1/admin/routing/policies/<id>` returns priority reversed. I can share curl of admin API if helpful.

support_julia: Example admin output after save: 
```
{"id":"p-789","priority":["us-west","eu-central"],"sticky":true,"sessionPin":true}
```
Before save it was ["eu-central","us-west"].

derek: Root-cause hypothesis: Console code uses Object.keys on a map when building the array and Node's iteration order edge-case reversed insertion order after some transform. I've seen this before in the serializer we rolled in 2025. We'll patch to use explicit stable ordering.

matt_sre: Action items: 1) Roll back routing-config-service to v5.0.1 to restore correct policy serialization. 2) Invalidate sticky KV for affected customers so new sessions get correct cookie. 3) Run canary to confirm eu-central becomes primary again. 4) Customer remediation: offer billing credit for egress and increased latency window.

anya: I'm starting the rollback now. Derek, please prioritize a patch for console serializer and a unit test covering priority order + sessionPin. Matt, prep an invalidate script for the affected account ids. Julia, please update the customer and ask for any extra logs.

ops-bot: Deploy-bot: routing-config-service rollback to v5.0.1 started at 2026-03-17T10:38:05Z.

support_julia: Customer says partial improvement after rollback but still seeing some 403s for sessions created during the bad window. They expect a timeline. I'm proposing: full rollback completed + KV invalidate + confirm 1h canary then close.

derek: I'll open a P0 on eng-runtime/console, PR incoming with fix + regression tests. Also adding a migration to re-serialize all policies and ensure stable ordering.

matt_sre: Invalidate script ran for acme-prod at 2026-03-17T10:44:12Z, cleared ~12k sticky entries. Waiting for metrics to settle.

support_julia: Customer notified and asking about refund. Attached suggested credit: prorated egress + partial SLA credit for the 90m window.

anya: Good. Keep this thread for updates. Once we confirm all clear, create postmortem with root cause, customer impact numbers (egress MB, 403 count, p90 increase).

support_julia: Will do. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
